draft.emotion: a sense of rushing or missed opportunity, often slightly anxious or apologetic
notes: Used with 'ser' to say it is late in the day (Ya es muy tarde — It's very late). Do not confuse with the feminine noun 'la tarde' (the afternoon).

senses.definition: After the expected, usual, or proper time, or near the end of the day.

examples.text: Llegué tarde a la reunión porque había mucho tráfico.
examples.translation: I arrived late to the meeting because there was a lot of traffic.
examples.emotion: slightly flustered and apologetic, explaining a delay

examples.translation: I went to sleep very late yesterday.

draftBefore.emotion: a sense of rushing or missed opportunity, often slightly anxious or apologetic
notes: As an adverb, 'tarde' can describe both a time of day and the status of being behind schedule.
Do not confuse this with the noun 'la tarde', which specifically refers to the afternoon period of the day.

senses.definition: After the expected or proper time.

examples.text: Llegué tarde a la reunión porque había mucho tráfico.
examples.translation: I arrived late to the meeting because there was a lot of traffic.
examples.emotion: slightly flustered and apologetic, explaining a delay

senses.definition: During the part of the day between noon and evening.

examples.text: Voy a estudiar un poco por la tarde.
examples.translation: I am going to study a little in the afternoon.
examples.emotion: calm and structured, planning out the day

faults.quote: (time) During the part of the day between noon and evening.
faults.why: 'Tarde' meaning 'afternoon' is a feminine noun ('la tarde'), not an adverb.

faults.quote: As an adverb, 'tarde' can describe both a time of day
faults.why: False grammar claim; 'tarde' only refers to the afternoon as a noun, contradicting note 1.
